ground_truth_root_cause: Deploy sha=49a7631b1ddb (2026-05-16T12:04:07Z) by Dónal O'Sullivan modified payment-service/config/cors.yaml and deploy/helm/payment-service/values.yaml as part of a profiling configuration change. During this edit, the cors.allowed_origins list was overwritten and the newly launched frontend subdomain https://checkout-v2.shop.example.com was omitted. The resulting config at startup only contains ["https://shop.example.com", "https://www.shop.example.com", "https://checkout.shop.example.com"], causing all CORS preflight requests from checkout-v2.shop.example.com to be rejected with HTTP 403, blocking payment submissions for all users on that subdomain.
ground_truth_remediation: 1. Immediately add 'https://checkout-v2.shop.example.com' to the cors.allowed_origins list in payment-service/config/cors.yaml and deploy/helm/payment-service/values.yaml. 2. Roll out a hotfix config-only deploy or use the Helm values override (e.g., helm upgrade payment-service ... --set cors.allowedOrigins[3]=https://checkout-v2.shop.example.com) to apply the fix without a full redeploy. 3. Restart or send a SIGHUP to payment-service pods to reload config. 4. Verify CORS rejections drop to zero for checkout-v2.shop.example.com in the next 2 minutes. 5. Add a config validation test that asserts all known frontend subdomains are present in the allowed origins list before merging config changes.
